Forecast Discussion

A dry front crosses the mountains this evening. It brings no rain, just the end of the warm stretch. High pressure settles into Pennsylvania this weekend. The weekend turns cooler with more clouds as the flow turns easterly. Spotty drizzle is possible Sunday night into Monday morning, mostly east near the Blue Ridge.

The high moves to the New England coast early next week, and the easterly flow continues. Spotty light rain or drizzle is possible Tuesday into Tuesday night, mostly on the east side of the Appalachians.

Low pressure forms over the central Plains Monday and moves into the Southeast by Wednesday. Light rain or drizzle develops from south to north Wednesday and increases Wednesday night.

The low is near Chattanooga early Thursday, and rain continues, especially in the morning. The low and its front move across the Southern Appalachians Thursday. The exact timing is difficult from this far out, but showers remain possible Thursday afternoon, becoming more focused on the west side of the mountains Thursday night in a northwest flow.
